column1: # kind|MM-DD|year|Greek name|English name|English biography   (English versions of the short biographies in data/bios; kind is always bio)

bio|01-12|1964|Τζεφ Μπέζος|Jeff Bezos|Jeff Bezos was born in New Mexico and in 1994 founded Amazon, at first as an online bookshop. The company became one of the largest in the world in online commerce and cloud services. He also founded the spaceflight company Blue Origin.

bio|01-12|1976|Άγκαθα Κρίστι|Agatha Christie|Agatha Christie was an English writer of detective novels. She created the detectives Hercule Poirot and Miss Marple and wrote works such as "Murder on the Orient Express". Her books have sold billions of copies and her play "The Mousetrap" has run for decades.

bio|01-12|2023|Λίζα Μαρί Πρίσλεϊ Αμερικανίδα τραγουδίστρια|Lisa Marie Presley|Lisa Marie Presley was an American singer and songwriter and the only daughter of Elvis Presley. She released albums as a performer and as a lyricist and was married to well-known figures of music and film. She died in 2023.

bio|01-13|888|Κάρολος ο Παχύς|Charles the Fat|Charles the Fat was king of the Franks and for a short time reunited a large part of the empire of Charlemagne. He could not cope with the Viking raids and was deposed in 887. He died in 888.

bio|01-13|1808|Σάλμον Π. Τσέις|Salmon P. Chase|Salmon Chase was an American politician from Ohio. He was an opponent of slavery, Secretary of the Treasury under Lincoln and later Chief Justice of the Supreme Court. Chase Bank was named after him.

bio|01-13|1864|Βίλχελμ Βίεν|Wilhelm Wien|Wilhelm Wien was a German physicist. He studied black-body radiation and formulated the displacement law that bears his name. In 1911 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics.

bio|01-13|1866|Γεώργιος Γκουρτζίεφ|George Gurdjieff|Georgi Gurdjieff was a teacher of spiritual search, of Caucasian origin. He taught a system he called the "Fourth Way" and founded an institute in France. His ideas influenced many writers and artists.

bio|01-13|1906|Αλέξανδρος Ποπόφ|Alexander Popov|Alexander Popov was a Russian physicist and electrical engineer. He experimented with wireless communication and built one of the first antennas for receiving electromagnetic signals. In Russia he is regarded as the inventor of radio.

bio|01-13|1924|Πωλ Φεγεράμπεντ|Paul Feyerabend|Paul Feyerabend was an Austrian philosopher of science. In his book "Against Method" he argued that there is no single method for the progress of science and defended "methodological anarchism".

bio|01-13|1941|Τζέιμς Τζόυς|James Joyce|James Joyce was an Irish writer. He wrote "Dubliners", "A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man" and "Ulysses", one of the most important works of modernism. He lived most of his years abroad and died in Zurich.

bio|01-13|1977|Ορλάντο Μπλουμ|Orlando Bloom|Orlando Bloom is an English actor. He became known as Legolas in "The Lord of the Rings" and as Will Turner in "Pirates of the Caribbean". He also appeared in the film "Troy".

bio|01-14|1861|Μωάμεθ ΣΤ΄|Mehmed VI|Mehmed VI was the last Ottoman sultan, from 1918 to 1922. When the Grand National Assembly of Ankara abolished the sultanate, he left the country on a British ship and died in exile in Italy.

bio|01-14|1867|Ζαν Ωγκύστ Ντομινίκ Ενγκρ|Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres|Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres was a French neoclassical painter. He was a pupil of David and is famous for his portraits and nudes, such as the "Grande Odalisque" and "The Bather". He was one of the leaders of academic painting.

bio|01-14|1875|Άλμπερτ Σβάιτσερ|Albert Schweitzer|Albert Schweitzer was born in Alsace and was a theologian, musician and physician. He founded a hospital at Lambaréné in Gabon, where he treated the local people. In 1952 he was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for his philosophy of "reverence for life".

bio|01-14|1898|Λιούις Κάρολ|Lewis Carroll|Lewis Carroll, whose real name was Charles Dodgson, was an English writer and mathematician. He wrote "Alice's Adventures in Wonderland" and its sequel "Through the Looking-Glass", among other works. He taught mathematics at Oxford.

bio|01-14|1919|Τζούλιο Αντρεόττι|Giulio Andreotti|Giulio Andreotti was an Italian Christian Democrat politician. He was prime minister seven times and a minister many times. He was tried for links with the mafia and was finally acquitted, and for decades he remained a central figure of Italian politics.

bio|01-14|1925|Γιούκιο Μισίμα|Yukio Mishima|Yukio Mishima was a Japanese writer and playwright. He wrote novels such as "Confessions of a Mask" and "The Temple of the Golden Pavilion". In 1970 he committed ritual suicide after a failed coup attempt.

bio|01-14|1957|Χάμφρεϊ Μπόγκαρτ|Humphrey Bogart|Humphrey Bogart was an American actor. He became famous with the films "Casablanca" and "The Maltese Falcon". He won an Oscar for "The African Queen". He died of cancer at fifty-seven.

bio|01-14|1963|Στίβεν Σόντερμπεργκ|Steven Soderbergh|Steven Soderbergh is an American director and producer. He began with the film "Sex, Lies, and Videotape", which won the Palme d'Or in 1989, and won the Oscar for Best Director for "Traffic".

bio|01-14|1978|Κουρτ Γκέντελ|Kurt Gödel|Kurt Gödel was born in Moravia and lived in the United States. He was a logician and mathematician and proved the incompleteness theorems, which changed the foundations of mathematics. He was a friend of Einstein at Princeton.

bio|01-15|69|Γάλβας|Galba|Galba was Roman emperor for about seven months, from June 68 to January 69. He was an old general and came to the throne after the death of Nero. He was murdered by the Praetorians and was succeeded by Otho.

bio|01-15|1519|Βάσκο Νούνιες ντε Μπαλμπόα|Vasco Núñez de Balboa|Vasco Núñez de Balboa was a Spanish conquistador. In 1513 he crossed the Isthmus of Panama and was the first European to see the Pacific Ocean from the American continent. He was arrested and executed in 1519.

bio|01-15|1622|Μολιέρος|Molière|Molière, whose real name was Jean-Baptiste Poquelin, was born in Paris. He was an actor and writer of comedies such as "Tartuffe", "The Misanthrope" and "The Miser". He also acted in his own plays at the court of Louis XIV.

bio|01-15|1809|Πιερ-Ζοζέφ Προυντόν|Pierre-Joseph Proudhon|Pierre-Joseph Proudhon was a French thinker and one of the first to call himself an anarchist. He wrote "What Is Property?", in which he argued that property is theft. He influenced socialist and anarchist movements.

bio|01-15|1876|Ιμπν Σαούντ|Ibn Saud|Abdulaziz Ibn Saud was the founder of Saudi Arabia. He captured Riyadh in 1902 and then united the regions of the Arabian Peninsula. In 1932 he proclaimed the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, of which he was the first king.

bio|01-15|1918|Γκαμάλ Άμπντελ Νάσερ|Gamal Abdel Nasser|Gamal Abdel Nasser was an officer who took part in the 1952 revolution in Egypt. He became president in 1956, nationalised the Suez Canal and emerged as a leader of Arab nationalism. He died in 1970.

bio|01-15|1919|Ρόζα Λούξεμπουργκ|Rosa Luxemburg|Rosa Luxemburg was born in Poland and became a Marxist thinker and revolutionary in Germany. She co-founded the Spartacus League and the Communist Party. She was arrested and murdered in Berlin on 15 January 1919.

bio|01-15|1919|Καρλ Λίμπκνεχτ|Karl Liebknecht|Karl Liebknecht was a German socialist politician and member of parliament. He opposed the First World War and together with Rosa Luxemburg founded the Spartacus League. He was arrested and murdered in 1919 during the Spartacist uprising.

bio|01-15|1929|Μάρτιν Λούθερ Κινγκ|Martin Luther King Jr.|Martin Luther King Jr. was an American pastor and leader of the civil rights movement for Black Americans. He supported nonviolent resistance, led the March on Washington in 1963 and was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1964. He was assassinated in 1968.

bio|01-16|1595|Μουράτ Γ΄|Murad III|Murad III was an Ottoman sultan from 1574 to 1595. During his reign the Ottomans fought Persia and the Habsburgs and the financial situation of the state became difficult. He was succeeded by his son Mehmed III.

bio|01-16|1794|Έντουαρντ Γκίμπον|Edward Gibbon|Edward Gibbon was an English historian. He wrote "The History of the Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire", published in six volumes from 1776 to 1789. The work is considered a classic of historiography.

bio|01-16|1901|Φουλχένσιο Μπατίστα|Fulgencio Batista|Fulgencio Batista was a Cuban military officer and politician. He ruled Cuba after a military coup in 1952 as a dictator. He was overthrown by the revolution of Fidel Castro and left the country on 1 January 1959.

bio|01-16|1931|Γιοχάνες Ράου|Johannes Rau|Johannes Rau was a German Social Democrat politician. He served as minister-president of North Rhine-Westphalia and from 1999 to 2004 as president of Germany. He died in 2006.

bio|01-16|1932|Νταϊάν Φόσεϊ|Dian Fossey|Dian Fossey was an American zoologist who studied the mountain gorillas of Rwanda. She founded a research centre and fought against poaching. She was found murdered in 1985, and her life became the film "Gorillas in the Mist".

bio|01-16|1933|Σούζαν Σόνταγκ|Susan Sontag|Susan Sontag was an American writer and essayist. She wrote essays on art and photography, such as "On Photography" and "Regarding the Pain of Others", and novels. She was a human rights activist.
bio|01-16|1979|Aaliyah|Aaliyah|Aaliyah was an American R&B singer and actress. She became famous in the late 1990s. She was killed in a plane crash in the Bahamas in 2001, at the age of twenty-two.

bio|01-16|2001|Λοράν Ντεζιρέ Καμπιλά|Laurent-Désiré Kabila|Laurent-Désiré Kabila was a Congolese rebel and politician. In 1997 he overthrew Mobutu and became president of the Democratic Republic of the Congo. He was assassinated in 2001 and was succeeded by his son Joseph.

bio|01-16|2014|Χίρου Ονόντα|Hiroo Onoda|Hiroo Onoda was a Japanese officer who continued to fight in the Philippines until 1974, because he did not believe that the Second World War had ended. He surrendered when his former commander ordered him to stop.

bio|01-17|1706|Βενιαμίν Φραγκλίνος|Benjamin Franklin|Benjamin Franklin was born in Boston. He was a printer, scientist, inventor and diplomat and one of the Founding Fathers of the United States. He invented the lightning rod, studied electricity and co-signed the Declaration of Independence.

bio|01-17|1893|Ράδερφορντ Χαίηζ|Rutherford B. Hayes|Rutherford B. Hayes was the 19th president of the United States, from 1877 to 1881. He was elected in a disputed election and withdrew federal troops from the South, ending Reconstruction. He was a former Civil War general.

bio|01-17|1899|Αλ Καπόνε|Al Capone|Al Capone was born in Brooklyn and became the boss of the Chicago mafia in the 1920s, in the era of Prohibition. He was convicted in 1931 of tax evasion and died in 1947.

bio|01-17|1942|Μοχάμεντ Άλι|Muhammad Ali|Muhammad Ali was born Cassius Clay and became three times world heavyweight boxing champion. He won an Olympic gold medal in 1960. He was known for his rhetoric and for his positions against the Vietnam War.

bio|01-17|1961|Πατρίς Λουμούμπα|Patrice Lumumba|Patrice Lumumba was the first prime minister of independent Congo, from June 1960. He was deposed and arrested and killed in January 1961, amid a crisis that included foreign interventions. He became a symbol of the African struggle for independence.

bio|01-17|1962|Τζιμ Κάρεϊ|Jim Carrey|Jim Carrey is a Canadian actor and comedian. He became known with films such as "Ace Ventura", "The Mask" and "The Truman Show". He also has dramatic roles, as in "Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind".

bio|01-17|1964|Μισέλ Ομπάμα|Michelle Obama|Michelle Obama was born in Chicago and studied law. She married Barack Obama and was First Lady of the United States from 2009 to 2017. She worked on healthy eating and the education of girls.
bio|01-17|2002|Καμίλο Χοσέ Θέλα|Camilo José Cela|Camilo José Cela was a Spanish writer. He wrote the novel "The Family of Pascual Duarte". In 1989 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|01-17|2008|Μπόμπι Φίσερ|Bobby Fischer|Bobby Fischer was an American chess player. In 1972 he won the world title, beating Boris Spassky in Reykjavik, in a match that became an international event of the Cold War. Later he lived most of his years in isolation.

bio|01-18|1689|Μοντεσκιέ|Montesquieu|Charles de Montesquieu was a French philosopher of the Enlightenment. In "The Spirit of the Laws" he argued for the separation of powers, an idea that influenced many constitutions. He also wrote the "Persian Letters".

bio|01-18|1862|Τζον Τάιλερ|John Tyler|John Tyler was the 10th president of the United States. He became president in 1841 after the death of Harrison and was the first vice-president to take office in this way. He supported the annexation of Texas.

bio|01-18|1873|Έντουαρντ Μπούλβερ-Λύττον|Edward Bulwer-Lytton|Edward Bulwer-Lytton was an English writer and politician. He wrote the historical novel "The Last Days of Pompeii" and was also known for his work in British politics.

bio|01-18|1904|Κάρι Γκραντ|Cary Grant|Cary Grant was born in Bristol, England, and became one of the greatest actors in Hollywood. He appeared in Alfred Hitchcock films such as "Notorious" and "North by Northwest" and in comedies such as "Bringing Up Baby". He was nominated twice for an Oscar and received an honorary Oscar in 1970.

bio|01-18|1936|Ράντγιαρντ Κίπλινγκ|Rudyard Kipling|Rudyard Kipling was born in India and was a British writer and poet. He wrote "The Jungle Book" and the poem "If". In 1907 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|01-18|1925|Ζιλ Ντελέζ|Gilles Deleuze|Gilles Deleuze was a French philosopher and professor. He wrote important works on philosophy and cinema and, with Félix Guattari, "Anti-Oedipus" and "A Thousand Plateaus". He committed suicide in 1995.

bio|01-18|1955|Κέβιν Κόστνερ|Kevin Costner|Kevin Costner is an American actor and director. He won the Oscar for Best Director for "Dances with Wolves". He also starred in "The Untouchables" and "Robin Hood: Prince of Thieves".

bio|01-18|1971|Ζοζέπ Γκουαρδιόλα|Josep Guardiola|Pep Guardiola was born in Catalonia and played as a midfielder for Barcelona. He became a coach and won many titles with Barcelona, Bayern and Manchester City. He is considered one of the leading coaches of his time.

bio|01-19|1736|Τζέιμς Βατ|James Watt|James Watt was born in Scotland and was an engineer. He greatly improved the steam engine, which helped the Industrial Revolution. The unit of power, the watt, was named after him.

bio|01-19|1798|Ογκίστ Κοντ|Auguste Comte|Auguste Comte was a French philosopher and is regarded as one of the founders of sociology. He developed positivism and argued that humanity passes through three stages: the theological, the metaphysical and the positive.

bio|01-19|1809|Έντγκαρ Άλαν Πόε|Edgar Allan Poe|Edgar Allan Poe was born in Boston. He was an American writer and poet and a pioneer of detective and horror fiction. He wrote the poem "The Raven" and stories such as "The Black Cat".

bio|01-19|1839|Πωλ Σεζάν|Paul Cézanne|Paul Cézanne was born in Aix-en-Provence, France. He was a post-impressionist painter and a pioneer of modern art. In his works, such as still lifes and landscapes, he analysed forms with simple geometric principles and opened the way to cubism.

bio|01-19|1865|Πιερ-Ζοζέφ Προυντόν|Pierre-Joseph Proudhon|Pierre-Joseph Proudhon died in Paris in 1865. He was a French thinker and one of the first anarchists. He influenced labour and socialist movements with his ideas of mutualism and federation.

bio|01-19|1946|Ντόλι Πάρτον|Dolly Parton|Dolly Parton is an American country singer and songwriter. She wrote the song "I Will Always Love You" and "Jolene" and has acted in films. She also founded a programme that sends books to children.

bio|01-19|1969|Γιαν Πάλαχ|Jan Palach|Jan Palach was a Czech student. On 16 January 1969 he set himself on fire in Prague in protest at the Soviet occupation after the Prague Spring and died three days later. He became a symbol of resistance.

bio|01-19|2000|Χέντι Λαμάρ|Hedy Lamarr|Hedy Lamarr was born in Vienna and became a Hollywood actress. She was also an inventor: together with the composer George Antheil she developed a frequency-hopping system that was later used in communications such as wifi.

bio|01-19|2007|Χραντ Ντινκ|Hrant Dink|Hrant Dink was an Armenian journalist in Turkey and editor of the newspaper "Agos". He supported reconciliation between Turks and Armenians. He was assassinated in Istanbul in 2007.

bio|01-20|1775|Αντρέ Μαρί Αμπέρ|André-Marie Ampère|André-Marie Ampère was a French physicist and mathematician. He developed the theory of electromagnetism and Ampère's law. The unit of electric current, the ampere, was named after him.

bio|01-20|1873|Γιοχάνες Βίλχελμ Γένσεν|Johannes V. Jensen|Johannes V. Jensen was a Danish writer. He wrote "The Long Journey" and in 1944 was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. His works combine history, nature and myth.

bio|01-20|1900|Τζον Ράσκιν|John Ruskin|John Ruskin was an English art critic and social thinker. He wrote "Modern Painters" and "The Stones of Venice" and defended Gothic architecture and artistic craftsmanship. He also influenced ideas of social reform.

bio|01-20|1920|Φεντερίκο Φελίνι|Federico Fellini|Federico Fellini was born in Rimini and became one of the greatest directors of Italian cinema. He directed "La Strada", "La Dolce Vita" and "8½". He won four Oscars for Best Foreign Language Film and an honorary Oscar.

bio|01-20|1930|Μπαζ Όλντριν|Buzz Aldrin|Buzz Aldrin is an American astronaut. In 1969, on the Apollo 11 mission, he was the second person to walk on the Moon, after Neil Armstrong. Before that he had flown as a fighter pilot.

bio|01-20|1936|Γεώργιος Ε΄|George V|George V was king of the United Kingdom and emperor of India from 1910 to 1936. He reigned during the First World War and changed the name of the royal house to Windsor. He was succeeded by Edward VIII.

bio|01-20|1990|Μπάρμπαρα Στάνγουικ|Barbara Stanwyck|Barbara Stanwyck was an American film and television actress. She became known with the films "Double Indemnity" and "Stella Dallas" and was nominated four times for an Oscar. She also starred in the television series "Dynasty".

bio|01-20|1993|Όντρεϊ Χέπμπορν|Audrey Hepburn|Audrey Hepburn was born in Brussels and became a Hollywood actress. She won an Oscar for "Roman Holiday" and also became known with "Breakfast at Tiffany's". In her last years she was a Goodwill Ambassador for UNICEF.

bio|01-21|1793|Λουδοβίκος ΙΣΤ΄|Louis XVI|Louis XVI was the last king of France before the French Revolution. He was arrested in 1792 and convicted of treason. He was beheaded by guillotine on 21 January 1793.

bio|01-21|1869|Γκριγκόρι Ρασπούτιν|Grigori Rasputin|Grigori Rasputin was a Russian peasant and mystic. He gained influence at the court of Tsar Nicholas II because the tsar's wife believed he helped her sick son. He was murdered in 1916 by nobles.

bio|01-21|1905|Κριστιάν Ντιόρ|Christian Dior|Christian Dior was born in Normandy. In 1946 he founded the fashion house Dior. His 1947 collection, called the "New Look", with a narrow waist and wide skirts, influenced the fashion of the time. He died in 1957.

bio|01-21|1924|Βλαντιμίρ Λένιν|Vladimir Lenin|Vladimir Lenin was a Russian revolutionary and leader of the Bolsheviks. He led the October Revolution of 1917 and became head of the Soviet government. He died in 1924 after strokes.

bio|01-21|1926|Καμίλλο Γκόλτζι|Camillo Golgi|Camillo Golgi was an Italian physician and scientist. He discovered a method of staining nerve cells and described the Golgi apparatus. In 1906 he shared the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine with Ramón y Cajal.

bio|01-21|1941|Πλάθιντο Ντομίνγκο|Plácido Domingo|Plácido Domingo was born in Madrid and is a tenor and conductor. He has sung in major opera houses and was one of the "Three Tenors" with Pavarotti and Carreras.

bio|01-21|1950|Τζορτζ Όργουελ|George Orwell|George Orwell, whose real name was Eric Blair, was a British writer. He wrote "Animal Farm" and "1984", two works about totalitarianism. He died of tuberculosis shortly after the publication of "1984".

bio|01-21|1953|Πολ Άλεν|Paul Allen|Paul Allen was an American businessman. He co-founded Microsoft in 1975 with his friend Bill Gates. He invested in many fields and owned sports teams. He died in 2018.

bio|01-21|1956|Τζίνα Ντέιβις|Geena Davis|Geena Davis is an American actress. She won the Oscar for Best Supporting Actress for "The Accidental Tourist" and was nominated for an Oscar for "Thelma & Louise". She also founded an institute for the representation of women in the media.

bio|01-22|1561|Φράνσις Μπέικον|Francis Bacon|Francis Bacon was an English philosopher and politician. He supported the inductive method and systematic observation as the basis of science. He wrote the "Novum Organum" and served as Lord Chancellor of England.

bio|01-22|1788|Λόρδος Βύρων|Lord Byron|Lord Byron was a British Romantic poet and wrote works such as "Childe Harold" and "Don Juan". He was a philhellene and came to Greece in 1823 to help the Revolution. He died of fever at Missolonghi in 1824.

bio|01-22|1849|Άουγκουστ Στρίντμπεργκ|August Strindberg|August Strindberg was a Swedish writer and playwright. He wrote the plays "Miss Julie" and "The Father" and the novel "The Red Room". He is considered a pioneer of naturalism and expressionism.

bio|01-22|1891|Αντόνιο Γκράμσι|Antonio Gramsci|Antonio Gramsci was an Italian philosopher and politician and one of the founders of the Italian Communist Party. He was imprisoned by Mussolini's regime and wrote the "Prison Notebooks", in which he developed the concept of cultural hegemony.

bio|01-22|1898|Σεργκέι Αϊζενστάιν|Sergei Eisenstein|Sergei Eisenstein was a Soviet director. He directed "Battleship Potemkin" and "Alexander Nevsky". He is considered a pioneer of the technique of montage in cinema.

bio|01-22|1901|Βικτώρια|Victoria|Victoria was queen of the United Kingdom from 1837 to 1901 and empress of India. Her long reign, the "Victorian era", was marked by industrial growth and the expansion of the empire. She died at Osborne House.

bio|01-22|1908|Λεβ Λαντάου|Lev Landau|Lev Landau was a Soviet theoretical physicist. He contributed to the study of superfluidity and the physics of condensed matter. In 1962 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics.

bio|01-22|1919|Καρλ Λάρσον|Carl Larsson|Carl Larsson was a Swedish painter. He became known for watercolours and murals with scenes of family life, particularly the series "A Home". He had great influence on Swedish art.

bio|01-22|1973|Λίντον Τζόνσον|Lyndon B. Johnson|Lyndon B. Johnson was the 36th president of the United States. He took office after the assassination of Kennedy in 1963. He promoted civil rights laws and the "Great Society" programme, but involvement in the Vietnam War reduced his popularity.

bio|01-22|2008|Χιθ Λέτζερ|Heath Ledger|Heath Ledger was an Australian actor. He became known with the films "Brokeback Mountain" and "The Dark Knight", in which he played the Joker. He received a posthumous Oscar for Best Supporting Actor. He died in 2008 at the age of twenty-nine.

bio|01-23|1516|Φερδινάνδος Β΄|Ferdinand II|Ferdinand II was king of Aragon. By his marriage to Isabella of Castile he united the two kingdoms and together they supported the voyage of Columbus. They completed the Reconquista with the capture of Granada in 1492.

bio|01-23|1783|Σταντάλ|Stendhal|Stendhal, whose real name was Henri Beyle, was a French writer. He wrote the novels "The Red and the Black" and "The Charterhouse of Parma". He is considered a pioneer of realism in literature.

bio|01-23|1832|Εντουάρ Μανέ|Édouard Manet|Édouard Manet was a French painter and a precursor of impressionism. He became known for works such as "Luncheon on the Grass" and "Olympia", which caused a scandal in their time. He influenced the impressionists.

bio|01-23|1862|Ντάβιντ Χίλμπερτ|David Hilbert|David Hilbert was a German mathematician. He contributed to geometry, algebra and the foundations of mathematics. In 1900 he presented a list of 23 unsolved problems that guided the mathematics of the 20th century.

bio|01-23|1907|Χιντέκι Γιουκάβα|Hideki Yukawa|Hideki Yukawa was a Japanese physicist. In 1935 he predicted the existence of the meson, a particle that holds the nucleus together. In 1949 he became the first Japanese person to win the Nobel Prize in Physics.

bio|01-23|1930|Ντέρεκ Γουόλκοτ|Derek Walcott|Derek Walcott was a poet and playwright from Saint Lucia in the Caribbean. He wrote the epic poem "Omeros", inspired by the Odyssey. In 1992 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. He died in 2017.

bio|01-23|1944|Έντβαρτ Μουνκ|Edvard Munch|Edvard Munch was a Norwegian painter. He became known with "The Scream", which expresses fear and anguish and is considered a symbol of expressionism. He dealt with themes of life, love and death.

bio|01-23|1989|Σαλβαδόρ Νταλί|Salvador Dalí|Salvador Dalí was a Spanish surrealist painter. He is known for paintings such as "The Persistence of Memory" with its melting clocks. He was also an eccentric public figure and died in Figueres, Catalonia.

bio|01-23|2015|Αμπντουλάχ|Abdullah|Abdullah was king of Saudi Arabia from 2005 to 2015. He supported limited reforms in the country and some initiatives for education and development. He was succeeded by his half-brother Salman.

bio|01-24|41|Γάιος Καλιγούλας|Caligula|Caligula was Roman emperor from 37 to 41. At first he was popular, but later he became known for his cruelty and eccentricities. He was assassinated by officers of his guard.

bio|01-24|76|Αδριανός|Hadrian|Hadrian was Roman emperor from 117 to 138. He travelled to all the provinces and built frontier walls, such as Hadrian's Wall in Britain. He loved Greece, carried out works in Athens and completed the Temple of Olympian Zeus.

bio|01-24|1712|Φρειδερίκος Β΄|Frederick II|Frederick II the Great was king of Prussia from 1740 to 1786. He strengthened the army and expanded the state, mainly by the conquest of Silesia. He was also a patron of the arts and a friend of Voltaire.

bio|01-24|1862|Έντιθ Γουόρτον|Edith Wharton|Edith Wharton was an American writer. She wrote novels about the high society of New York, such as "The Age of Innocence", for which in 1921 she became the first woman to win the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction.

bio|01-24|1920|Αμεντέο Μοντιλιάνι|Amedeo Modigliani|Amedeo Modigliani was an Italian painter and sculptor who lived in Paris. He made portraits and nudes with elongated faces and necks. He died young, at thirty-five, and recognition came after his death.

bio|01-24|1940|Γιοάχιμ Γκάουκ|Joachim Gauck|Joachim Gauck was born in Rostock and was a pastor and an opposition activist in East Germany. In 2012 he became president of Germany and remained until 2017.
